\section{Threshold Functions --- Gaussian}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.Gaussian
\subsection*{Threshold Functions --- Gaussian: Introduction}
The quantitative Gaussian approximation statements and correlated-Gaussian quadrant formula lead to regular-threshold and majority noise-stability bounds.

\subsection*{Threshold Functions --- Gaussian: Results}

\begin{definition}[Kolmogorov distance of real measures]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.kolmogorovDistance}
\leanok
For measures $\mu,\nu$ on $\mathbb R$, define $D_K(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\mu(({-\infty},t])-\nu(({-\infty},t])|$, taking the real value of each measure mass, assigning real value zero to infinite mass, and assigning supremum zero if the displayed set is unbounded. For probability measures this is the usual Kolmogorov distance.
\end{definition}

  {BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p118-b005}
\proofstep
  {BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.kolmogorovDistance}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p118-b005}
There exists a real constant $c\ge0$ such that the following holds. For every natural
number $n$, every probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, and every family of real random
variables $(X_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)}$ that is mutually independent, measurable, has
integrable third absolute powers, has mean zero term by term, and has total second
moment equal to $1$, the Kolmogorov distance between the distribution of $\sum_i X_i$
and the standard Gaussian measure is at most $c\sum_i\int |X_i|^3\,d\mu$.
\end{theorem}

  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b002}
There is a real constant $C\geq0$ such that for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every family of
real coefficients $(a_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,n}$, and every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, if
$\sum_i a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\leq\varepsilon$ for every $i$, then
\[\left|\mathbb E\left|\sum_i a_i\sigma(X_i)\right|-\sqrt{2/\pi}\right|\leq C\varepsilon,\]
where $X$ is uniform on the Boolean cube and $\sigma$ is the sign encoding.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Lower-left probability of a Gaussian pair]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianQuadrantProbability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p016-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b002,
  pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p003-b004
}
Let $G,H$ be independent standard real Gaussians. For every real $\rho$, define $Q(\rho)=\Pr[G\le0,\ \rho G+\sqrt{\max(1-\rho^2,0)}\,H\le0]$; when $|\rho|\le1$, the two displayed coordinates form a standard Gaussian pair of correlation $\rho$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{5}
Let $G,H$ be independent standard real Gaussian random variables, and let
$-1\le\rho\le1$. The probability that $G\le0$ and $\rho G+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,H\le0$ is
$\frac12-\frac{\arccos(\rho)}{2\pi}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stability of regular linear threshold functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.regular_ltf_stability}

  {BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.abs_thresholdSign}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b002}
There is a real constant $C\geq0$ such that for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every real-valued
function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, every coefficient family $(a_i)_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,n}$, and
every $\varepsilon,\rho\in\mathbb R$, the following holds. If $f(x)$ is the threshold
sign, with zero assigned sign $1$, of $\sum_i a_i\sigma(x_i)$ for every $x$, this sum is
nonzero for every $x$, $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, $|a_i|\leq\varepsilon$ for every $i$, and
$|\rho|<1$, then
\[\left|\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)-\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin\rho\right|\leq\frac{C\sqrt{\varepsilon}}{1-\rho},\]
where $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)$ is the inner product of $f$ with its noise operator
at parameter $\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Majority stability decreases to the Gaussian limit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_stability_limit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_noiseStability_antitone, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability, BooleanAnalysis.majority}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p121-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p054-b005
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p008-b001}
\difficulty{4}
There exists a universal real constant $C\ge0$ such that for every $0\le\rho<1$, the majority function $M_k$ on $2k+1$ uniform bits, equal to $1$ when $\sum_i(-1)^{x_i}>0$ and $-1$ otherwise, satisfies $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_{k+1})\le\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_k)$ for all $k\ge0$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_k)\to(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho$ as $k\to\infty$. For every integer $k\ge0$, $(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho\le\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_k)\le(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho+C/(\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\sqrt{2k+1})$. For a real function $h$ on a uniform bit cube, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(h)=\sum_S\rho^{|S|}\widehat h(S)^2$.
\end{theorem}

For every $0<\rho<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $\tau>0$ such that for all $n\ge0$ and $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ with uniform mean zero and $I_i(f)\le\tau$ for every $i$, one has $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)\le(2/\pi)\arcsin\rho+\varepsilon$. Here $I_i(f)=\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^{\{i\}}))^2]/4$, where $x^{\{i\}}$ flips bit $i$. For a real function $h$ on a uniform bit cube, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$, and $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(h)=\sum_S\rho^{|S|}\widehat h(S)^2$.
\end{theorem}
